items.stem: The middle most observation of every data arranged in order is called
items.answer: When all the observations are arranged in ascending or descending order, the observation lying in the middle is the median. Hence the middle most observation is called the median.

items.stem: For some data x₁, x₂, ...............xₙ with respective frequencies f₁, f₂, ......fₙ, the value of Σ₁ⁿ fᵢ(xᵢ − x̄) is equal to
items.answer: Σfᵢ(xᵢ − x̄) = Σfᵢxᵢ − x̄Σfᵢ. Since x̄ = Σfᵢxᵢ / Σfᵢ, we have x̄Σfᵢ = Σfᵢxᵢ, so the difference is 0. Hence Σfᵢ(xᵢ − x̄) = 0.

items.stem: The median and mode respectively of a frequency distribution are 26 and 29, Then its mean is
items.answer: By the empirical relation Mₒ = 3M_d − 2M, with Mₒ = 29 and M_d = 26: 29 = 3 × 26 − 2M, so 2M = 78 − 29 = 49 and M = 49/2 = 24.5. The mean is 24.5.
items.concept: Empirical relation of the three measures

items.stem: The cumulative frequency table is useful in determining
items.answer: A cumulative frequency table is a running total of the frequencies. From it the mean, the median and the mode of the distribution can all be found, so it is useful in determining all of these.

items.stem: In a frequency distribution, the mid value of a class is 10 and the width of the class is 6. The lower limit of the class is
items.answer: Let x be the upper limit and y the lower limit. The mid value gives (x + y)/2 = 10, i.e. x + y = 20. The width gives x − y = 6. Solving the two equations, y = 7. The lower limit of the class is 7.

items.stem: For finding the popular size of readymade garments, which central tendency is used?
items.answer: The popular size is the size that occurs most often, and the measure of central tendency that picks the most frequent value is the mode. Hence mode is used.

items.stem: If the difference of mode and median of a data is 24, then the difference of median and mean is
items.answer: Given Mₒ − M_d = 24. Using Mₒ = 3M_d − 2M, Mₒ − M_d = 2M_d − 2M = 2(M_d − M). So 24 = 2(M_d − M) and M_d − M = 12. The difference of median and mean is 12.
items.concept: Empirical relation of the three measures

items.stem: If the mean of the numbers 27 + x, 31 + x, 89 + x, 107 + x, 156 + x is 82, then the mean of 130 + x, 126 + x, 68 + x, 50 + x, and 1 + x is
items.answer: From the first set, 82 = (410 + 5x)/5, so 410 + 5x = 410 and x = 0. The second set then sums to 130 + 126 + 68 + 50 + 1 + 5x = 375, and its mean is 375/5 = 75.

items.stem: The median of a set of 9 distinct observations is 20.5. If each of the largest 4 observation of the set is increased by 2, then the median of the new set

options.label: C
options.text: Is two times the original median

options.label: D
options.text: Remains the same as that of the original set

items.answer: With n = 9 the median is the ((9 + 1)/2)th = 5th observation. Increasing only the largest four observations does not disturb the first five in order, so the 5th observation is unchanged. The median remains the same as that of the original set.

items.stem: If the coordinates of the point of intersection of less than ogive and more than ogive is (13.5,20), then the value of median is
items.answer: The two ogives meet at the point whose abscissa is the median of the data. The abscissa of (13.5, 20) is 13.5, so the median is 13.5.

items.stem: A set of numbers consists of three 4's, five 5's, six 6's, eight 8's and seven 10's. The mode of this set of numbers is
items.answer: The mode is the value with the highest frequency. Here 8 occurs eight times, more often than 4 (three times), 5 (five), 6 (six) or 10 (seven). Hence the mode is 8.

items.stem: If the mean of the observation x, x + 3, x + 5, x + 7 and x + 10 is 9, the mean of the last three observation is
items.answer: The five observations sum to 5x + 25, so 9 = (5x + 25)/5, giving x = 4. The last three observations are x + 5, x + 7 and x + 10, summing to 3x + 22 = 34. Their mean is 34/3 = 11⅓.

items.stem: The mean and median of the data a, b and c are 50 and 35 respectively, where a < b < c. If c − a = 55, then (b − a) is
items.answer: As a < b < c, the median is the middle value b, so b = 35. The mean gives a + b + c = 150, hence a + c = 115. With c − a = 55, subtracting gives 2a = 60, so a = 30. Therefore b − a = 35 − 30 = 5.

items.stem: Observations of some data are x/5, x, x/3, 2x/3, x/4, 2x/5 and 3x/4 where x > 0. If the median of the data is 4, then the value of x is
items.answer: In ascending order the seven observations are x/5, x/4, x/3, 2x/5, 2x/3, 3x/4, x. With n = 7 the median is the 4th observation, which is 2x/5. So 2x/5 = 4, giving x = 20/2 = 10.

items.stem: If the mean of the squares of first n natural numbers is 105, then the first n natural numbers is
items.answer: The sum of the squares of the first n natural numbers is n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6, so the mean of the squares is (n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 = 105. This gives 2n² + 3n − 629 = 0, i.e. (2n + 37)(n − 17) = 0, so n = 17. Since 17 is odd, the median of the first 17 natural numbers is the ((17 + 1)/2)th = 9th observation, which is 9.

items.stem: While computing the mean of grouped data, we assume that the frequencies are

options.label: A
options.text: evenly distributed over all the classes

options.label: B
options.text: centred at the class marks of the classes

options.label: C
options.text: centred at the upper limits of the classes

options.label: D
options.text: centred at the lower limits of the classes

items.answer: In the grouped mean each class is represented by its class mark, which amounts to assuming that the whole frequency of a class is concentrated at its class mark. Hence the frequencies are taken as centred at the class marks of the classes.

items.stem: If median is 137 and mean is 137.05, then the value of mode is
items.answer: By the empirical relation Mₒ = 3M_d − 2M = 3(137) − 2(137.05) = 411 − 274.10 = 136.90. The mode is 136.90.
items.concept: Empirical relation of the three measures

Then, find the average expenditure which is done by the maximum number of manual workers.
items.answer: The expenditure of the greatest number of workers is the mode. The maximum frequency 40 belongs to 1500-2000, so l = 1500, h = 500, f₁ = 40, f₀ = 24 and f₂ = 33. Then Mₒ = 1500 + (40 − 24)/(80 − 24 − 33) × 500 = 1500 + 16/23 × 500 = 1847.26.

items.stem: If X, M and Z are denoting mean, median and mode of a data and X:M = 9:8, then the ratio M:Z is
items.answer: The empirical relation gives Z = 3M − 2X. From X:M = 9:8, X = 9M/8. Hence Z = 3M − 2(9M/8) = 3M − 9M/4 = 3M/4, so M/Z = 4/3, i.e. M : Z = 4 : 3.
items.concept: Empirical relation of the three measures

items.stem: If the mean of a, b, c is M and ab + bc + ca = 0, the mean of a², b² and c² is KM², then K is equal to
items.answer: From the mean, a + b + c = 3M, and (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca) = a² + b² + c² since ab + bc + ca = 0. So a² + b² + c² = 9M². The mean of the squares is 9M²/3 = 3M², and comparing with KM² gives K = 3.

items.stem: In the formula x̄ = a + (Σfᵢdᵢ)/(Σfᵢ), for finding the mean of grouped data dᵢ's are deviation from a of
items.answer: In the assumed-mean method each class is represented by its class mark xᵢ = (upper limit + lower limit)/2, and dᵢ = xᵢ − a. So the deviations are taken from a of the mid-points of the classes.

options.label: C

items.answer: Each class in a grouped distribution is represented by its class mark, so the frequency of a class is taken to be concentrated there. The frequencies are centred at the class marks of the classes.

items.stem: If xᵢ's are the mid-points of the class intervals of grouped data, fᵢ's are the corresponding frequencies and x̄ is the mean, then Σ(fᵢxᵢ − x̄) is equal to
items.answer: Σ(fᵢxᵢ − x̄) = Σfᵢxᵢ − nx̄. Since x̄ = (Σfᵢxᵢ)/n, we get nx̄ = Σfᵢxᵢ, so the expression equals Σfᵢxᵢ − Σfᵢxᵢ = 0.

items.stem: In the formula x̄ = a + h((Σfᵢuᵢ)/(Σfᵢ)), for finding the mean of grouped frequency distribution, uᵢ is equal to
items.answer: In the step-deviation method the deviation of the class mark from the assumed mean is divided by the class size, so uᵢ = (xᵢ − a)/h.

items.stem: The mean weight of 9 students is 25 kg. If one more student is joined in the group the mean is unaltered, then the weight of the 10ᵗʰ student is
items.answer: The nine students weigh 25 × 9 = 225 kg in all. If the mean is still 25 kg for ten students, the new total is 25 × 10 = 250 kg, so the tenth student weighs 250 − 225 = 25 kg. Adding a value equal to the mean never changes the mean.

items.stem:
Assertion : If the number of runs scored by 11 players of a cricket team of India are 5, 19, 42, 11, 50, 30, 21, 0, 52, 36, 27 then median is 30.
Reason : Median = ((n + 1)/2)ᵗʰ value, if n is odd.
items.assertion: If the number of runs scored by 11 players of a cricket team of India are 5, 19, 42, 11, 50, 30, 21, 0, 52, 36, 27 then median is 30.
items.reason: Median = ((n + 1)/2)ᵗʰ value, if n is odd.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.

items.answer: Arranging the runs in ascending order gives 0, 5, 11, 19, 21, 27, 30, 36, 42, 50, 52. With n = 11 (odd) the median is the ((11 + 1)/2)ᵗʰ = 6ᵗʰ value, which is 27, not 30. So the assertion is false, while the reason states the correct rule and is true.
